about.intro: Every line of code, every merge, every fix. On GitHub it all adds up to numbers and green squares — but behind those squares are late nights, false starts, and hard-won progress. Green Wall is where those stories get told.
about.whyWeBuiltContent:
We spend our days deep in code and issues, and rarely stop to look back at how far we've come.
Maybe you've forgotten the night you finally cracked that bug, or the PR you rewrote after it got rejected.
Those small moments add up — they made you the developer you are today.
Green Wall turns that contribution wall into a record of your own growth: something you can see, and something worth sharing.
about.howItHelps: How it helps you tell your story
about.howItHelpsIntro: Green Wall isn't just an image generator. It pulls your contributions on GitHub together and turns them into:
about.howItHelpsItem1: Clear visuals — every day, every week, every year at a glance.
about.howItHelpsItem2: Sharing that fits you — pick the theme, size, and style that match how you want to be seen.
about.howItHelpsItem3: More than a picture — a highlight for your README, or hard evidence of your work for a job application, a portfolio, or a quiet look back at your own year.
about.inspirationContent:
This tool started with one question: what if your contributions could be hung like a painting?
It reads your data through GitHub's official API and renders it into a wall, right in the browser.
about.finalMessageContent:
Every line you write isn't just a commit — it's part of your story.
Green Wall makes sure those stories don't fade away, so they become something you're proud of.
Generate your wall, and let people see the work behind it.
about.supportContent: If Green Wall makes your work feel a little more visible, you can support it by giving it a star on <github>GitHub</github> or an upvote on <productHunt>Product Hunt</productHunt>. Telling a friend, or adding it to your portfolio, helps too.
about.reportingIssuesContent: Found a bug, have an idea, or spotted something that could feel smoother? Open an issue on <link>GitHub</link>. We read every one.
